subject: Varying Widths across a stacked bar chart

messages.subject: Varying Widths across a stacked bar chart
parts:
Hi, I've done research and have seen users of ggplot coerce geom_rect() into having variable widths across a barchart, however my question is a bit more involved.

My goal is to create a stacked bar chart underneath a curve that takes the form of f(x) = x^.5. The stack charts below the function will have varying widths and heights as the curve increase and finally flattens out as X increases. So, there is a curve and with varying heiths and widths in a stacked fashion beneath it.

I am under the impression that something like the following call would do the trick to take care of the stacked portion of the plot:

ggplot(RevSpend, aes(CostPerBin, revBin, fill = x))  + geom_bar(aes(CostPerBin, revBin),stat = "identity", position='stacked')

I also understand that there will be many many more additions to the code, but the error that I run into that surrounds using the stacked argument is that the widths must be constant. 

Is there a way to trick ggplot into interpreting the widths as constant without changing the underlying variable that is to be plotted?


I can provide much more information, I just don't know if this email list is expecting code/data/etc.


-M
